extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting, structuring, and polishing short stories (roughly 1,000–7,500 words), with emphasis on character-driven conflict, economy, and scene-level execution. Covers idea generation through revision and a final checklist of craft criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protagonist with a clear desire or need
rubrics_metrics.description: The story centers on a protagonist who has a clear want or need driving action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the protagonist's desire/need explicit in terms of motivation so the reader understands why the character acts; distinguish 'want' (often contrary to best interests) from 'need' (authentic benefit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-defined dilemma
rubrics_metrics.description: The protagonist faces a clear dilemma that creates the central tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dilemma should force choices and illuminate character, providing stakes and urgency that propel the plot toward the climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision made by protagonist (agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: The protagonist must make a significant decision; the story is driven by that active choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid passive plots where things happen to the character; the climax should center on a choice or action the protagonist takes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climactic moment where tension peaks
rubrics_metrics.description: The story builds to a single climactic moment of highest tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the rising tension so scenes increase charge toward this peak; the climax should resolve (or reframe) the central dilemma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome showing protagonist transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: The ending should demonstrate how the protagonist has changed (or failed to change) because of the events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transformation can be internal or external but should feel earned by the story's action and choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality in execution, not just premise
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality presents itself in storytelling, not necessarily in the initial idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on unique voice, scene choices, character perspective, and execution rather than obsessing over finding a wholly new idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character development before/with outlining
rubrics_metrics.description: Either outline the story or develop characters (background, motivations, fatal flaw) before drafting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep a small cast; know characters' motivations and fatal flaw so scenes naturally arise from who they are rather than from plot contrivances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenes organized around conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Every scene should relate to the central struggle and contain conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid filler scenes; each scene should advance or regress the protagonist's progress toward goals and increase the story's 'charge.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish the first draft (prioritize completion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete a full first draft without getting stuck on perfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept imperfection in the initial draft; focus on creating forward momentum and building cumulative tension toward the climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise with fresh eyes and ruthless trimming
rubrics_metrics.description: Step away and then revise to ensure every word serves the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate anything that doesn't advance character, conflict, or theme; demand economy and purposeful phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a checklist for final assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the finished story against the craft checklist to find remaining problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically verify elements such as POV consistency, scene charge, pacing, and voice before submission or publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended word count: 1,000–7,500 words
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimal short-story length is between 1,000 and 7,500 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this range as a guideline for pacing and plot scope; shorter flash or longer novellas require different structural choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single time period focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the story within one primary time period; only use time gaps for travel or sleep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sprawling temporal jumps; if you do jump time, signal it clearly (space breaks) and limit frequency to preserve economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene-location economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Each scene should take place in a single location or continuous transit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid multi-location scenes that confuse the reader; maintain spatial clarity so the scene's action and stakes are immediate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use space breaks between time jumps
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert space breaks or other clear markers when the narrative jumps in time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves reader orientation and prevents confounding scene continuity across time shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single POV character
rubrics_metrics.description: Use one point-of-view character for the story (with rare Romance exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit internal access to one consciousness to maintain intimacy and clarity; exceptions must be deliberate and justified by structure or genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never head-hop
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not switch internal viewpoint within scenes or scenes without clear boundary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Head-hopping confuses readers and dilutes emotional engagement; maintain a stable vantage point per scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid narrating other characters' thoughts
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't report other characters' interior states directly; if needed, qualify with words like 'apparently,' 'obviously,' or 'supposedly.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use description, behavior, and dialogue to suggest others' minds rather than stating them; qualifiers help keep perspective honesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent internal access
rubrics_metrics.description: Be consistent about how much internal access the chosen POV allows throughout the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you use deep third or first person, maintain that level of interiority; avoid slipping into omniscient narration unless established.

rubrics_metrics.name: One clear protagonist who transforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Center on a single protagonist who typically undergoes transformation by story's end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus emotional investment and structural momentum on this character; secondary characters support or obstruct their change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined antagonist creating obstacles
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be a clear antagonist force—person, society, nature, or internal flaw—that creates obstacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make obstacles concrete and meaningful; the antagonist's opposition should clarify stakes and test the protagonist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protagonist begins trapped in a flaw
rubrics_metrics.description: Start the story with the protagonist constrained by a flaw or limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This flaw should motivate struggle and be the engine for potential change; let plot choices expose and challenge it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Want vs Need distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate between what the protagonist wants (surface desire) and what they truly need (authentic benefit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the story arc to reveal how pursuing the 'want' conflicts with the 'need' and how crisis forces recognition or failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene-level goals shown each scene
rubrics_metrics.description: Every scene should show the main character pursuing a clear goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state (by action/dialogue) what the character hopes to achieve in the scene so progress and stakes are readable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenes must carry 'charge' (progress/regression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each scene should have charge — it either advances the protagonist or causes regression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design scenes so they alter the character's situation or understanding; static scenes weaken momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most scenes end negatively until the climax
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow most scenes to conclude unfavorably for the protagonist until the climactic reversal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative scene endings maintain tension and underscore stakes; occasional wins are okay but should be meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear inciting incident
rubrics_metrics.description: An inciting incident must trigger the protagonist's visible story goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the inciting incident early and make its consequences unavoidable so the protagonist is compelled to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis compels change of approach
rubrics_metrics.description: A crisis should force the protagonist to alter strategy or perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The crisis must be consequential and reveal character under pressure, leading to a meaningful decision at the climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive character voice and dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters should speak distinctly and authentically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use diction, rhythm, and subtext to differentiate speakers; avoid generic dialogue that fails to reveal personality or motive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue should carry subtext
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogue must convey underlying tensions and unspoken intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid on-the-nose exposition; let characters imply truths through what they choose to say or omit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters should feel real, not author-illustrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters must be believable individuals rather than mouthpieces for the author's ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground characters in sensory detail, contradiction, and autonomy; avoid using them solely to argue a thesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat supporting characters acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting characters may be less developed if they serve the story efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor characters can be schematic if they fulfill a clear function, but avoid caricature that distracts the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succinct, fresh, specific prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Language should be economical, fresh, exciting, specific, and colorful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prune redundancy, choose vivid specifics, and prefer verbs that show action rather than abstract nouns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid clichés
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on clichéd phrasing, images, or plot beats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek original metaphors and precise descriptions to keep prose lively and avoid reader fatigue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vary sentence structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use varied sentence length and structure for rhythm and emphasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short sentences can heighten tension; longer sentences can slow pace for reflection—use both deliberately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre prose conventions (simple, direct symbolism)
rubrics_metrics.description: For genre stories, prefer simple language, short sentences, and direct symbolism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genre readers expect clarity and forward momentum; avoid overwrought language that stalls plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary prose conventions (sophisticated, metaphorical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary stories can employ sophisticated vocabulary, layered metaphor, and implied motifs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguity and layered meaning are acceptable, but still demand economy and internal logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use classic story structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider Three-Act structure or Freytag's Pyramid for story architecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These archetypes help pace exposition, rising action, climax, and resolution; adapt them to fit your story's needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie up threads in genre fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre stories typically resolve plot threads and explain necessary facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers of genre fiction expect closure on key plotlines; unanswered mysteries should be intentional and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow ambiguity in literary fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary stories may leave certain elements unresolved or ambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguity must feel purposeful and thematically resonant rather than careless or evasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental forms require internal logic
rubrics_metrics.description: If using experimental structure or form, it must maintain a clear internal logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventive forms are allowed only if readers can perceive consistent rules and feel oriented within them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hook the reader at the beginning
rubrics_metrics.description: Open the story with a compelling hook—mystery, distinctive voice, vivid location, or humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early engagement is vital; avoid slow expository openings that delay the central question or voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep exposition to a minimum; show rather than tell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveal necessary backstory and context only when it becomes relevant and earned by the reader's curiosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid distancing phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use distancing words/phrases like 'used to' or 'would often'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These constructions can detach readers from immediacy; prefer present-tense action and direct description when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earn backstory after reader wants answers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide backstory only after the reader is engaged and wants to know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay explaining everything; let curiosity motivate revelation to preserve tension and discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain high stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the story's stakes are significant to the protagonist (emotional, relational, physical, or moral).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakes don't have to be epic, but they must matter deeply to the central character and affect choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every sentence should compel the next
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for prose where each sentence is compelling enough to urge the reader to continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim or rework lines that stall momentum; make each sentence earn its place in the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy: no subplots
rubrics_metrics.description: Short stories require economy—avoid subplots; every element should serve the central conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus the narrative on one core conflict and eliminate secondary plotlines that dilute emotional impact or pacing.
